pillars.title: Sorted on upload
pillars.body: Every file lands in a category with its source, its date and its people already read off the page. Contracts, chats, receipts, photographs, official records.

pillars.title: Screenshots become searchable
pillars.body: Text inside a Messenger capture is extracted, so a search for the amount or the promise finds the thread instead of you opening four hundred images.

pillars.title: A timeline with sources attached
pillars.body: Each entry carries the files it came from and a confidence figure. Click any date to see exactly what the app read.
pillars.detail: Chronology drafts from the same data.

pillars.title: Proof matrix per cause of action
pillars.body: Pick the case type and the elements appear beside the evidence you actually have, with the gaps named before you file rather than at trial.

steps.title: Drop the whole folder in
steps.body: Screenshots, phone photos, scanned contracts, bank PDFs, email exports. The intake reads each file once and records where it came from and when it was captured.

steps.title: Bad copies are flagged before anything is read
steps.body: Blur, glare, low resolution, cropped pages, rotation and shadow are detected first. You are told which files need a clearer copy instead of finding out in court.

steps.title: Files sort themselves into evidence categories
steps.body: Contracts, receipts, chats, photographs, affidavits and official records, each with the source named. A GCash receipt is filed as a GCash receipt, not as IMG_4471.

steps.title: Text comes out with a confidence figure per field
steps.body: Amounts, dates, reference numbers, names and signatures are extracted as separate fields. Anything below the threshold is left blank and marked for review rather than guessed.

steps.title: Dated events, each tied to its files
steps.body: The timeline is assembled from what was extracted. Every entry lists its sources and its confidence, so a weak date is visible as a weak date.

steps.title: A chronology written from the timeline
steps.body: Narrative paragraphs with citations to the evidence behind each sentence. It is a first draft for a statement of facts, not a filing.

steps.title: Exhibit letters proposed in order
steps.body: Each proposed exhibit carries the purpose it would be offered for. Re-letter or reject any of them.

steps.title: Names picked up from the documents themselves
steps.body: Signatories, affiants, officers and people mentioned in chats, with the files they appear in so you can see why a name was suggested.

steps.title: Statements that do not sit together are flagged
steps.body: A denial in a counter-affidavit against an admission in a chat. A payment dated before the contract. The app raises them and stops. You decide whether it matters.

steps.title: Documents you do not have yet
steps.body: Missing items are listed against the element they would support, with a note on where that document is normally obtained.

steps.title: Proof matrix for the cause of action
steps.body: Elements on the left, your evidence beside them, status on the right. The unsupported rows are the ones to fix before filing.

steps.title: Trial binder and hearing view
steps.body: Per witness: purpose, proposed questions and the documents to bring. The hearing view holds one setting, its issues, its exhibits and its reminders.

confidenceBands.label: Read cleanly
confidenceBands.meaning: Quoted directly, used in the timeline without a warning.

confidenceBands.label: Review recommended
confidenceBands.meaning: Included and usable, marked so you check the field before you rely on it.

confidenceBands.label: Not relied upon
confidenceBands.meaning: Kept in the case file, never quoted as fact, and listed in the review queue with the reason.

safeguards.title: It says what it cannot read
safeguards.body: An unreadable amount is reported as unreadable. There is no fallback to a plausible figure.

safeguards.title: The original is never overwritten
safeguards.body: Deskew, contrast and rotation produce a separate enhanced view. The file as uploaded stays untouched.

safeguards.title: Corrections stay in the record
safeguards.body: When you type in a name the extraction missed, the entry is marked as manually entered, with who entered it and when.

safeguards.title: Cross-references are offered, not concluded
safeguards.body: If a blurred receipt matches a bank transfer and a chat, all three are shown side by side and the verification is left to you.

safeguards.title: Every fact traces back
safeguards.body: No timeline entry, chronology sentence or exhibit exists without the files behind it.

safeguards.title: It does not give legal advice
safeguards.body: No opinion on the merits, no recommendation to file or settle. Organisation and extraction only.

faq.q: Does it decide anything about the case?
faq.a: No. It sorts files, extracts text, builds a timeline and lays your evidence against the elements of the cause of action you pick. Whether an inconsistency matters, whether to file, and what to argue are yours.

faq.q: What happens with a blurry screenshot?
faq.a: It is kept in the case file and marked so that nothing is quoted from it. The reasons are listed as detected, for example motion blur or a resolution of 640 by 480, and you are asked for a clearer copy.

faq.q: Does it read Filipino and Taglish?
faq.a: Yes. Threads in Filipino, English and mixed usage are extracted as written, without translation. Quoted text stays in the language of the original.

faq.q: How does this sit with the Data Privacy Act?
faq.a: Case files hold personal and sometimes sensitive personal information, so the office remains the personal information controller. On Chambers, processing can be kept within a Philippine region and retention rules are set per client. Review your own data processing agreement before uploading client files.

faq.q: Which causes of action have a proof matrix?
faq.a: BP 22, estafa, collection of sum of money, unlawful detainer and forcible entry, and copyright and trademark infringement. Each matrix lists its own basis so you can check the formulation used.

faq.q: Can I correct what it extracted?
faq.a: Yes, on any field. The correction is recorded as manually entered with the name of whoever entered it and the time, and it stays in the audit trail.
